title: hotfix: stabilize-slo-enforcer-backoff-ordering-urgent
author: Aisha Patel
description: Urgent hotfix to address a regression in the SLO enforcer backoff ordering that surfaced during a regional failover and burst load on 2026-02-14. Symptom: under certain failover/redispatch scenarios the enforcer re-queued requests in non-deterministic order, which allowed higher-cost requests to bypass backoff windows and caused cascading load-shedding and SLO violations across regions. Impact: customer-facing latency SLOs breached in us-west and eu-west, increased error budget consumption, and automated autoscaling thrashing. Root cause: race between the regional failover request reconcilation path and the per-customer backoff queue where re-enqueue used wall-clock insertion instead of monotonic ordering plus missing hysteresis when region tokens were refilled. Changes introduced: 1) ensure deterministic re-enqueue ordering by attaching monotonic sequence IDs at admission and using them for queue ordering in slo-enforcer; 2) add hysteresis to the regional backoff refill logic to avoid immediate refill thrashing; 3) add a small per-region token-bucket cap when reconciling failover targets to avoid burst amplification; 4) tighten backoff intervals for high-cost routes and add a safety cutoff to prevent infinite retry loops; 5) add targeted unit tests, integration scenario for failover+burst, and an e2e canary in us-west. Implementation touches slo-enforcer core queue and regional-failover controller, plus a small runtime config change and two new tests in integration/failover. Testing and rollout: local unit test coverage added for queue ordering and hysteresis; integration tests replicate the incident pattern and pass in CI; deployed as a canary to us-west with synthetic traffic and real traffic shadowing for 2 hours before global rollout. This PR is intentionally minimal and isolates the ordering and hysteresis fixes to avoid changes to scheduling or batching heuristics. Checklist: [x] reproduce failure locally with integration harness; [x] deterministic unit tests; [x] CI green (integration); [x] canary validation in us-west; [x] post-merge monitoring runbook updated. Related: Linear ENG-6321 (incident followup), ENG-6399 (slo-enforcer backlog).
